name: Hidden Topology and Inaccessible Continuation Domains Law
purpose: Define inaccessible continuation domains as bounded reconstruction and accessibility phenomena.

candidate_law_statement.informal: A continuation structure may remain stable without being reconstructively accessible from a given local continuation domain.

formal.hidden_domain_candidate: H_A(α) := { β : β ∉ D_A(α) or reconstruction_fidelity(α,β) < θ_Ξ }
formal.hidden_topology_candidate: Top_H(U) := continuation topology weakly accessible, inaccessible, compressed, fragmented, or reconstructively ambiguous relative to U
formal.inaccessibility_condition: Inaccessibility may arise through finite-flux decay, admissibility horizon formation, topology fragmentation, perturbation corruption, or arbitration pruning.
formal.partial_trace_condition: A hidden domain may leave indirect traces, perturbation signatures, compression residues, or invariant distortions without full reconstruction accessibility.
formal.nonabsolute_hiddenness_clause: Hiddenness is local and reconstruction-conditioned, not absolute or metaphysically privileged.
formal.nonobserver_completion_clause: No observer, reconstruction process, or admissibility domain is assumed capable of complete global topology recovery.
